q1: SELECT name FROM drinker WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT f.bar FROM frequents AS f, serves AS s WHERE f.drinker = drinker.name AND f.bar = s.bar AND NOT s.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM likes WHERE drinker = drinker.name))
q2: WITH drinkerLikes AS (SELECT DISTINCT drinker.name, likes.beer FROM drinker JOIN likes ON drinker.name = likes.drinker), barServes AS (SELECT DISTINCT bar.name, serves.beer FROM bar JOIN serves ON bar.name = serves.bar), drinkerFreq AS (SELECT DISTINCT drinker, bar FROM frequents), likesServes AS (SELECT DISTINCT barServes.name, barServes.beer FROM barServes JOIN drinkerLikes ON drinkerLikes.beer = barServes.beer), onlyServesLikes AS (SELECT likesServes.name FROM likesServes GROUP BY name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT beer) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT beer) FROM barServes AS bs WHERE bs.name = likesServes.name)) SELECT * FROM onlyServesLikes

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for drinkers who do not serve any beer that they like, while Q2 identifies bars that serve only the beers that their regular customers like.
counterexample_dsp: A bar that serves a beer which no regular customer of that bar likes.
